title: Rotate Image
summary: Given an n x n 2D matrix representing an image, rotate the image 90 degrees clockwise in-place without using an additional matrix.
statement: Given an n x n 2D matrix representing an image, rotate the image 90 degrees clockwise in-place without using an additional matrix.
constraints: A square matrix with side length 1–20 and values between -1000 and 1000.
Rotate 90 degrees clockwise by modifying matrix directly. Do not allocate a second matrix. The judge reads matrix after the call, not a returned copy.
hints: A clockwise rotation can be decomposed into a transpose followed by reversing each row.
Swap across the main diagonal once per pair, then reverse each row in place.
For row r, swap positions (r,c) and (c,r) only for c>r. Then reverse the contents of every row.
Swapping every diagonal pair twice cancels the transpose; allocating and returning a copy does not mutate the input.
editorial: Transpose by exchanging the upper-triangle cells with their lower-triangle partners, then reverse each row. These two reflections map each original (r,c) to (c,n-1-r), a clockwise quarter-turn. Both transformations modify the original matrix using constant auxiliary storage. The oracle constructs a separate output directly from the coordinate formula.

tests.explanation: The first column [1,4,7] becomes the top row in reverse order [7,4,1]; the other columns transform the same way.
The new top row is [15,13,2,5], and the new bottom row is [16,7,10,11].
